inferior lobar artery of right lung: Inferior lobar artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to the lower lobe of the right lung.
inferior medial genicular artery: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.
inferior mesenteric artery: Arises from the aorta at L3; supplies the hindgut (distal 1/3 of the transverse colon, descending and sigmoid colon, upper rectum).
inferior mesenteric vein: Drains the left colon and upper rectum and opens into the splenic vein.
inferior ophthalmic vein: Drains the floor of the orbit; connected with the pterygoid plexus.
inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery: First branch of the superior mesenteric artery; anastomoses with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.
inferior papillary muscle of left ventri: Posterior papillary muscle of left ventricle
Holds the mitral valve; because it has a single blood supply (usually the right coronary), it tends to rupture after infarction.
inferior papillary muscle of right ventr: Posterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
Papillary muscle holding the posterior and septal cusps of the tricuspid valve.
inferior petrosal sinus: Connects the cavernous sinus with the internal jugular vein; sampled in the diagnosis of Cushing's disease.
inferior phrenic artery: First branch of the abdominal aorta; supplies the diaphragm and gives the superior suprarenal artery.
inferior sagittal sinus: Lies in the free lower edge of the falx cerebri.
inferior suprarenal artery: Branch of the renal artery to the lower part of the adrenal gland.
inferior thyroid artery: Supplies the thyroid and parathyroids; closely related to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
inferior ulnar collateral artery: Joins the anastomosis above the elbow.
inferior vein of left ventricle: Drains the posterior surface of the left ventricle.
inferior vein of left ventricle (//poste: Posterior vein of left ventricle (accessory branch)
Additional drainage branch of the posterior surface of the left ventricle.
inferior vena cava (abdominal part): Formed at L5 by the union of the common iliac veins; rises to the right of the aorta.
inferior vena cava (thoracic part): Short part that passes through the diaphragm at T8 and opens into the right atrium.
infra-orbital artery: Runs through the floor of the orbit and emerges on the face at the infraorbital foramen.
insular branches of middle cerebral arte: The M2 segment branching over the surface of the insula.
Insular branches of middle cerebral artery (M2)
The M2 segment running over the insula.
intercapitular veins of foot: Connect the plantar and dorsal veins at the bases of the toes.
internal carotid artery: Gives no branches in the neck; passes through the carotid canal and cavernous sinus to supply the anterior circulation of the brain and the eye.
internal iliac artery: Supplies the pelvic organs, buttock and perineum; may be ligated in postpartum haemorrhage.
internal jugular vein: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus; runs in the carotid sheath and is often used for central venous catheters.
internal pudendal artery: Runs with the pudendal nerve in Alcock's canal; supplies the perineum and external genitalia.
internal thoracic artery: Descends 1 cm lateral to the sternal border; the graft most used in coronary bypass (LIMA).
internal thoracic veins: Veins accompanying the internal thoracic artery.
intrarenal arteries of left kidney: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate and interlobular arteries.
intrarenal arteries of right kidney: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate and interlobular arteries.
intrarenal veins of left kidney: The venous network inside the kidney.
intrarenal veins of right kidney: The venous network inside the kidney.
lacrimal artery: Supplies the lacrimal gland and the eyelids.
lateral basal segmental artery of left l: Lateral basal segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
lateral basal segmental artery of right: Lateral basal segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
lateral circumflex femoral artery: Supplies the anterolateral muscles of the thigh.
lateral circumflex femoral veins: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
lateral frontobasal artery: Supplies the inferolateral surface of the frontal lobe.
lateral occipital artery: Supplies the inferior surface of the temporal lobe.
lateral plantar artery: The large terminal branch; forms the deep plantar arch.
lateral plantar veins: Drain the lateral part of the sole.
lateral pontine branches of basilar arte: Lateral pontine branches of basilar artery
Supply the lateral parts of the pons.
lateral segmental artery of right lung: Lateral segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
lateral tarsal artery: Supplies the lateral part of the dorsum of the foot.
lateral thoracic artery: Supplies serratus anterior and the lateral part of the breast.
lateral vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
left atrium: The most posterior chamber of the heart, receiving oxygenated blood from four pulmonary veins; lies against the oesophagus (its enlargement can cause dysphagia).
left brachiocephalic vein: Long vein crossing obliquely in front of the branches of the aortic arch.
left common carotid artery: Arises directly from the aortic arch; runs in the carotid sheath of the neck with the internal jugular vein and vagus nerve.
left coronary artery: Short trunk from the left aortic sinus; divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex arteries. Its occlusion causes an extensive anterior infarction.
left coronary leaflet: The left coronary artery arises from the sinus behind it.
left gastric artery: The smallest branch of the coeliac trunk; supplies the lesser curvature of the stomach and the lower oesophagus and may be the source of bleeding ulcers.
left gastro-omental vein: Drains the left part of the greater curvature of the stomach.
left inferior pulmonary vein: Carries blood from the left lower lobe to the left atrium; isolated in atrial fibrillation ablation.
left pulmonary artery: Short branch that passes over the left main bronchus to the left lung.
left renal artery: Short artery to the left kidney; renal artery stenosis causes renovascular hypertension.
left renal vein: Passes between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery to reach the IVC (compression: nutcracker syndrome); receives the left gonadal and adrenal veins.
left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valv: Left semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
The left semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.
left subclavian artery: Arises directly from the aortic arch; if blocked before the origin of the vertebral artery, subclavian steal syndrome develops.
left subclavian vein: The thoracic duct opens into the left venous angle (its junction with the internal jugular).
left subcostal vein: Helps to form the hemiazygos vein.
left superior intercostal vein: Carries the left 2nd–4th intercostal veins to the left brachiocephalic vein.
left superior pulmonary vein: Carries blood from the left upper lobe and lingula to the left atrium.
left testicular artery: Long thin artery supplying the left testis.
left testicular vein: Opens into the left renal vein at a right angle; this is why varicocele is mostly left-sided.
left ventricle: The chamber with the thickest wall, forming the apex of the heart; pumps blood into the aorta.
lingular vein of left lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
long posterior ciliary arteries: Supply the iris and ciliary body.
lumbar arteries: Four pairs of segmental branches from the back of the aorta; supply the posterior abdominal wall and spine.
marginal artery: Chain of anastomoses along the edge of the colon joining the mesenteric arteries; weak at the splenic flexure (Griffiths' point, ischaemic colitis).
maxillary artery: Large terminal branch of the external carotid; in the infratemporal and pterygopalatine fossae it gives branches to the teeth, muscles of mastication, nose and dura.
maxillary veins: Veins coming from the pterygoid plexus.
medial basal segmental artery of left lu: Medial basal segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
medial basal segmental artery of right l: Medial basal segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
medial circumflex femoral artery: Winds round the back of the femoral neck and is the main supply of the femoral head; its injury in neck fractures causes avascular necrosis.
medial circumflex femoral veins: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
medial occipital artery: Gives the calcarine and parieto-occipital branches.
medial plantar artery: Small terminal branch supplying the medial part of the sole.
medial plantar veins: Drain the medial part of the sole.
medial pontine branches of basilar arter: Medial pontine branches of basilar artery
Perforating branches supplying the middle of the pons.
medial segmental artery of right lung: Medial segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
medial vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
median antebrachial vein: Drains the front of the forearm.
median cubital vein: Links the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa; the vein most used for taking blood.
median sacral artery: Thin artery arising behind the bifurcation and descending in front of the sacrum.
mental branch of inferior alveolar arter: Mental branch of inferior alveolar artery
Emerges at the mental foramen and supplies the chin.
middle cardiac vein: Runs in the posterior interventricular groove and opens into the coronary sinus.
middle cerebral artery (m1-segment): Continuation of the internal carotid; runs in the lateral fissure. Its lenticulostriate branches supply the internal capsule; occlusion causes marked paralysis of the opposite face and arm and (on the dominant side) aphasia.
middle cerebral artery (m3 segment): Segment on the inner surface of the opercula.
middle cerebral artery (m3-segment): The opercular segment, from which the cortical branches arise.
middle colic artery: Supplies the transverse colon in the transverse mesocolon.
middle collateral artery: Joins the anastomosis around the elbow.
middle lobar artery of right lung: Middle lobar artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to the middle lobe of the right lung.
middle meningeal artery: Enters the skull through the foramen spinosum; torn in pterion fractures, causing an epidural haematoma (lucid interval).
musculophrenic artery: Supplies the diaphragm and the lower intercostal spaces.
musculophrenic veins: Drain the margin of the diaphragm.
mylohyoid branch of inferior alveolar ar: Mylohyoid branch of inferior alveolar artery
non-coronary leaflet: The aortic cusp behind which no coronary artery arises.
obturator artery: Passes through the obturator canal to the thigh; sometimes arises from the external iliac artery ('corona mortis', dangerous in hernia surgery).
occipital artery: Supplies the back of the neck and the posterior scalp.
occipital sinus: Small sinus in the falx cerebelli.
occipital vein: Drains the scalp of the back of the head.
ophthalmic artery: First branch of the internal carotid; enters the orbit through the optic canal and supplies the eye, retina, forehead and part of the nose.
orbitofrontal branches of anterior cereb: Orbitofrontal branches of anterior cerebral artery
Supply the orbital surface of the frontal lobe.
palmar carpal branch of radial artery: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery
palmar digital veins: Drain the palmar surface of the fingers.
palmar metacarpal arteries: Branches arising from the deep arch.
parietal branches of middle cerebral art: Parietal branches of middle cerebral artery
Supply the lateral surface of the parietal lobe.
patellar anastomosis: Network of genicular arteries around the patella.
perforating branches of plantar metatars: Perforating branches of plantar metatarsal arteries
Branches joining the arteries of the sole with those of the dorsum of the foot.
perforating femoral arteries: Branches that pierce adductor magnus to supply the posterior thigh muscles.
perforating veins: Valved veins connecting the superficial and deep veins; their incompetence contributes to varicose veins.
pericallosal artery: Branch of the anterior cerebral artery running over the corpus callosum.
pericardium: Two-layered sac around the heart and the roots of the great vessels: the fibrous pericardium outside and the serous pericardium, with parietal and visceral layers, inside. Attached below to the central tendon of the diaphragm and in front to the sternum; a rapid rise of fluid between the layers causes cardiac tamponade.
plantar arch: Arch formed by the lateral plantar artery and the deep plantar artery.
plantar digital veins: Drain the plantar surface of the toes.
